cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 14 since November 2014. A practicing attorney and certified public accountant with accounting and law degrees, he is Vice Chair of the House Judiciary Committee. He lives in Arley.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to Alabama. We found no statements from him on data centers, development or growth limits, restrictions on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, abortion, gun policy, or policing and public order. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026. The pages we had did not show his sponsored bills, so we could not confirm any specific deeds on the platform issues. His campaign site makes claims about his record, such as the grocery tax cut, that we could not check against official records. His 2026 campaign finance totals were not available to us.

qual.background: Alabama House member since 2014 (12 years) and Judiciary Committee Vice Chair. He is a certified public accountant and has practiced tax law, with a B.S. and M.Acc. from the University of Alabama and a J.D. from Cumberland School of Law.
qual.why: He has more than a decade of legislative service and a law, tax and accounting career that fits writing law and the state budget. Committee posts were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has more than a decade of legislative service and a law, tax and accounting career that fits writing law and the state budget. Committee posts were not counted toward the score.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: He says he helped cut the state grocery tax from four percent to two percent, raised the state standard deduction and pushed higher business personal property tax exemptions. These are statements about tax relief generally, not homestead property tax relief, and he does not mention homestead taxes specifically.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: He says he will keep funding local public schools and community colleges. His campaign pages do not mention vouchers, charters, school choice or teacher pay.
